The car was being driven by R1.
Deceased was sitting in front beside driver.
R1 was driving the car rashly and negligently and hit the car into another vehicle going ahead on the road and caused horrible accident due to which deceased sustained multiple injuries.
Deceased was brought to District Hospital, Sonipat where he was declared dead due to injuries sustained in the accident.

There were four persons in the car beside respondent no. 1 i.e. deceased Rahul Mishra who was sitting on the co- driver seat in front.
Nikhil Chugh and Manish Yadav were sitting on the back seat of the car.
The said car collided with the Canter on the way back from Murthal where they were celebrating birthday of the common friend i.e. Sachin Jain.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

sentences.text: PW-2 in his affidavit Ex. PW 2/A deposed that on 21.05.2012 at about 1:30 AM, he was standing at Baliyan Petrol Pump, GT road, Murtha Sonipat and was waiting for a bus to reach home.
Suddenly, the offending car being driven by the driver in rash and negligent manner coming from Murthal side of the road, hit into a Canter which was going ahead of the car.
The driver and the occupant of the car received grievous injuries.
Someone informed the police.
Police took three persons to the hospital.
Later on, he came to know that one person namely Rahul Mishra (deceased)
who was one of the occupants in the car died due to the injuries sustained in the accident on the way to hospital.
18. In his cross-examination, PW-2 admitted that he did not go to the spot of the accident nor had taken the injured to the hospital.
He further admitted that he had not filed any police complaint nor made any call at 100 number to report the accident.
He failed to produce any bus ticket to show that he traveled by bus on the night of accident.
He also admitted that he did not note down the number of Canter with which the accident of Car had taken place.
19. The petitioner neither in her petition nor in her evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW 1/A has disclosed that the accident was witnessed by PW-2, Jitender.
Petitioner has failed to explain how she came to know that PW-2 is eye-witness of the accident.
PW-2 in his affidavit Ex. PW 2/A has also failed to explain how he came into contact with the petitioner and told her about the accident.
PW-2 did not disclose where he was working at the time of accident.

PW-2 deposed that he was MACT Case No. 206/20 (FIR no. 121/2012) Smt. Manoj Mishra Vs. Prateek Narang & Anr.

sentences.text: In the FIR No. 121/12, PS Murthal, Sonipat, police has filed untraced report.
Ld. Counsel for the respondent argued that the untrace report has been accepted by the Ld. Magistrate.

The petitioner herself has relied on the untrace report Ex. PW 1/6 wherein it has been submitted by the police that during the investigation that the driver and the Canter (offending vehicle) remained untraced.
No protest petition has been filed by the petitioner in the concerned Court.

If petitioner was aware about the eye-witness of the accident i.e. PW-2 then why she did not move appropriate application against respondent no. 1 before the concerned Court to punish the real culprit.
There is no document on record to corroborate the testimony of PW-2.
In view of the above discussion, the testimony of PW-2 is not trustworthiness and cannot be relied upon.

21. On the other hand, respondent no. 1 in his affidavit RW1/A deposed that the vehicle in front of his car was being driven in rash manner, and it suddenly applied the brakes to avoid the head on collision with the said vehicle, R1 applied the brakes and turned the car towards the right side.
He was not driving the car in rash manner.

sentences.text: The accident occurred on 21.05.2012.
The present petition has been filed only on 08.10.2020.
There is delay of more than 8 years in filing the present petition.

It has been mentioned in the petitiion that the petition could not be filed early because the younger son of the petitioner also got injured in road accident in Noida on 19.01.2016 and the papers of the present accident were not available with the petitioner.
These reasons are not satisfactory for explanation of delay in filing the petition.
The delay of 8 years in filing the present petition has not been satisfactory explained and therefore the false implication of respondent no. 1 in this case cannot be ruled out.
23. The initial burden lies on the petitioner to prove the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the driver/ respondent no. 1.

Reliance in this regard can be placed upon the findings in the case of Surender Kumar Arora & Anr. V. Manoj Bisla & Ors. (2012) 4 SCC 552, where in The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held as under:
"9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, the petition filed by the claimants was under Section 166 of the Act and not under Section 163-A of the Act.
This is not in dispute.

Therefore, it was the entire responsibility of the parents of the deceased to have established that respondent no.1 drew the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner which resulted in the fatal accident.
Maybe, in order to help respondent no.1, the claimants had not taken up that plea before the Tribunal.
Therefore, High Court was justified in sustaining the judgment and order passed by the Tribunal.
We make it clear that if for any reason, the claimants had filed the petition under Section 163-A of the Act, then the dicta of this Court in the case of Kaushnuma Begum (Smt.) & Ors.
(supra) would have come to the assistance of the claimants.

6 10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In our view the issue that we have raised for our consideration is squarely covered by the decision of this Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. (supra).

In the said decision the Court stated :
"27. ....Therefore, the victim of an accident or his dependants MACT Case No. 206/20 (FIR no. 121/2012) Smt. Manoj Mishra Vs. Prateek Narang & Anr.
Page no. 9 of 10 have an option either to proceed under Section 166 of the Act or under Section 163-A of the Act.
Once they approach the Tribunal under Section 166 of the Act, they have necessarily to take upon themselves the burden of establishing the negligence of the driver or owner of the vehicle concerned.

But if they proceed under Section 163-A of the Act, the compensation will be awarded in terms of the Schedule without calling upon the victim or his dependants to establish any negligence or default on the part of the owner of the vehicle or the driver of the vehicle."

24. In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is of considered opinion that the petitioner has failed to discharge the onus to prove that the accident was caused by rash and negligent driving of offending car by R1.
Therefore, the issue is decided in favor of the respondents and against the petitioner.
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
OPP 25.
Since, the petitioner has failed to prove the first prerequisite for invoking the Section 166 MV Act, petitioner is not entitled for compensation.
ISSUE NO. 3/ RELIEF 26.
In view of the finding of issue no. 1 and 2, the present petition is dismissed.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
